headline: Keep the target inside an inclusive search interval
statement: Given ascending nums with distinct integer values and a target, return its index if present, or -1 otherwise. Use logarithmic time.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
constraints: Values and target lie between -10^4 and 10^4.
intuition: Checking the middle divides sorted candidates into two halves. If the middle value is too small, every value before it is too small too; if too large, everything after it is too large. Exclude the middle after a failed comparison.
approach: While left<=right, compare nums[mid] to target.
Return mid for equality; otherwise keep only the possible half.
correctness: The invariant is that any occurrence lies in left..right. Sortedness justifies removing the middle and all smaller values when nums[mid]<target, or the middle and all larger values otherwise. If equality is found the returned index is correct. An empty interval proves absence.
bruteForce: A sequential scan takes O(n) time and cannot exploit sortedness.

complexity.explanation: Each comparison at least halves the interval, with only scalar boundaries.

pitfalls: Use <= so a final single candidate is tested.
Remove mid with +1 or -1 after a failed comparison to guarantee progress.
Return an index, not the target value.
Python integers do not overflow when computing (left+right)//2. In a fixed-width integer language, left+(right-left)//2 avoids addition overflow.
